title: Performance Prediction of On-NIC Network Functions with Multi-Resource Contention and Traffic Awareness
problem: Co-located network functions (NFs) on SmartNICs suffer performance interference from multi-resource contention (CPU cores, memory bandwidth, DMA engines, queues), but existing performance prediction models lack SmartNIC-specific knowledge and traffic-pattern awareness, yielding poor prediction accuracy for SLA management. Operators cannot efficiently allocate SmartNIC resources without accurate contention-aware performance predictions.
method: The paper develops a performance prediction framework that models SmartNIC-specific resource contention by profiling the interactions between co-located NFs across multiple resource dimensions (CPU, memory, interconnects). The model incorporates traffic awareness by accounting for how arrival patterns and traffic rates influence queuing delays and per-NF throughput under contention. Machine learning or analytical models (details from abstract) are used to predict NF latency and throughput given a resource allocation and traffic profile.

title: 20.3 An RFID-Inspired One-Step Packaged Multimode Bio-Analyzer with Vacuum Microfluidics for Point-of-Care Diagnostics
problem: Point-of-care (POC) biomarker detection today relies on paper-based lateral-flow assays (LFAs)—offering speed but poor quantitative accuracy—or centralized lab instrumentation that is bulky/expensive. Integrating CMOS with microfluidics faces packaging complexity (wire/flip-chip bonding) and requires external pumps/tubing.
method: RFID-inspired one-step packaged integration merges millimeter-scale CMOS circuits with vacuum-based microfluidics (eliminating syringe pumps). Multimode detection combines electrochemical, optical, or impedance sensing per target biomarker. Vacuum microfluidics passively transports samples without external actuation.

title: Hardware-Software Co-Design of Iterative Filter-Update Numerical Methods Using Processing-In-Memory
problem: Data movement is a critical bottleneck in machine learning and scientific computing; even pruning/filtering approaches require reading entire datasets to determine subsets.
method: Hardware-software co-design for iterative filter-update methods: (1) domain-specific language (DSL) for filter/update patterns, (2) PIM hardware with limited compute, (3) mapping to PIMEval simulator.

title: Effective Memory Management and Sparse Aware Cache for Row-Wise Sparse CNNs
problem: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are used in several image processing tasks like image recognition and object localization
method: implemented on very resource-constrained hardware, where processors are restricted in the amount of cache available

title: AutoRE: Bayesian-Optimization-based Automatic Reliability Enhancement Tool for Flow-based Microfluidic Biochips
problem: Flow-based microfluidic biochips suffer from low yield due to manufacturing defects causing malfunctions; while reliability quantification models exist, automatic layout optimization to enhance reliability is lacking.
method: AutoRE uses Bayesian optimization to explore layout variants within predefined topology constraints, identifying the most reliable configuration. The system varies spatial dimensions and positions without changing connectivity.

title: Comparing Distributed-Memory Programming Frameworks with Radix Sort
problem: Distributed-memory programming frameworks vary significantly in their capabilities for managing communication and synchronization overhead, making it difficult to evaluate trade-offs between scalability, productivity, and performance.
method: Implemented distributed radix sort (communication-intensive algorithm) across five programming frameworks (Chapel, MPI, OpenSHMEM, Conveyors, Lamellar) and measured performance, scalability, and code complexity on HPE Cray systems.

title: ABMF: Adaptive Bonsai Merkle Forests for Efficient Integrity Verification in Secure Persistent Memories
problem: Non-volatile memory security verification using Merkle trees requires expensive tree traversal for MAC and counter updates on every memory write, creating significant latency and performance overhead.
method: Forest structure extending Bonsai Merkle Trees by identifying intermediate tree nodes as additional root nodes. Extra roots maintained in secure processor reduce effective tree height for updates and verification.

title: Assessing a RISC-V Accelerator for Cross-Section Lookup in Chipyard
problem: Monte Carlo neutron transport simulations bottlenecked on cross-section lookups; Doppler broadening computations via Faddeeva function expensive in software
method: Custom RISC-V accelerator integrated with RocketCore in Chipyard; pipelined design using Humlidek 8th-order rational approximation for Faddeeva function; performance comparison with software RISC-V and Intel Core i5 Tiger Lake-U

title: Avalanche: Optimizing Cache Utilization via Matrix Reordering for Sparse Matrix Multiplication Accelerator
problem: Sparse Matrix Multiplication (SpMM) accelerators suffer from poor on-chip memory utilization due to irregular memory access patterns; existing designs fail to cache both input matrices efficiently, leading to redundant DRAM accesses and low throughput.
method: Avalanche applies three complementary techniques: (1) Mat-Reorder reorders columns of matrix B to maximize data locality and enable early completion of row computations in matrix A; (2) DP-Evict (Dead-Product Early Eviction) immediately evicts fully-computed intermediate products from on-chip SRAM to reclaim capacity; (3) RM-Caching (Reuse Distance-Aware Matrix Caching) prioritizes retention of matrix B elements with short reuse distances in the on-chip cache. Together these techniques keep both operand matrices resident in a 6.15 mm2 chip with minimal spill-to-DRAM.

title: Enabling the syscall_intercept library for RISC-V
problem: syscall_intercept library provides high-performance system call interception on x86, PowerPC, ARM but not RISC-V; missing functionality hinders RISC-V research and system development requiring syscall manipulation.
method: Port syscall_intercept to RISC-V Linux: design decisions for RISC-V architecture, implementation of user-space interception (no superuser required), evaluation on RISC-V systems.

title: Scaling the memory wall using mixed-precision - HPG-MxP on an exascale machine
problem: Most scientific simulations are memory bandwidth-limited; applicability of mixed-precision to sparse matrix workloads remains unclear
method: Optimized HPG-MxP benchmark implementation on exascale systems with algorithm enhancements for mixed-precision computation

title: Efficient Recycling Subspace Truncation Method for Periodic Small-Signal Analysis
problem: Krylov subspace recycling for periodic small-signal RF analysis accelerates simulation but increasing memory cost becomes a bottleneck in large-scale designs; restarting loses recycling benefits.
method: Proposes recycling subspace truncation framework with efficient initial guess selection method and Floquet-based subspace truncation strategy to reduce memory while maintaining iteration benefits.

title: Hopps: Leveraging Sparsity to Accelerate Automata Processing
problem: Automata processing (AP) workloads execute many finite state machines (FSMs) in parallel over streaming symbol data, but existing AP accelerators suffer poor utilization because most FSMs are inactive (in a non-matching state) for any given input symbol. The irregular, state-dependent activation pattern makes it hard to exploit spatial parallelism efficiently.
method: Hopps exploits the observation that only a sparse subset of FSMs transition on each input symbol. It uses a sparsity-aware representation that tracks only active states across all FSMs and a compressed activation bitmap to skip idle FSMs entirely during each symbol step. The architecture couples this with a tiled SRAM storage layout so that state-transition tables for active FSMs are fetched in bursts, reducing off-chip memory traffic proportional to the active-FSM fraction.

title: SeIM: In-Memory Acceleration for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
problem: ANNS workloads bottleneck on memory bandwidth (extensive random access) and sorting (cross-memory-unit data dependencies), limiting throughput in CPU/GPU/ASIC-based systems and making them inefficient for RAG-based LLM inference.
method: Hierarchical in-memory architecture that offloads memory-bound parallel ANNS operations (vector loading, distance computation) to the memory bank level with minimal DRAM modifications, and places compute-bound sorting at the memory controller level with adaptive transmission filtering to reduce cross-unit data transfers during merge operations.

title: DHAP: Towards Efficient OLAP in a Disaggregated and Heterogeneous Environment
problem: Data systems lack adequate support for combining two key datacenter trends: hardware disaggregation and heterogeneous accelerators. Existing systems handle only homogeneous disaggregated CPUs or heterogeneous accelerators within monolithic servers.
method: End-to-end framework with query compiler and specialized runtime. Compiler's planning module identifies efficient execution plans; lower levels generate code for heterogeneous backends. Runtime handles inter-stage pipelined execution, minimizes communication costs, and respects local memory constraints.

title: 15.2 A 1024-Channel 0.00029mm2/ch 74nW/ch Online Spatial Spike-Sorting Chip with Event-Driven Spike Detection and Self-Organizing Map Clustering
problem: High-density multi-electrode arrays (HD-MEA) for brain-computer interfaces generate massive raw spike data that must be reduced on-chip for wireless operation. Prior spike-sorting (SS) designs either require large input buffers, use temporal features that don't scale to multi-channel systems, access entire clustering memory per spike, or consume high power and area.
method: A 1024-channel spike-sorting chip uses event-driven spike detection (only processes spike events, not raw samples) and spatial spike-sorting (uses waveform shape, not time features) with self-organizing map (SOM) clustering. Event-driven and spatial approaches avoid large buffers, scale to multi-channel systems, and eliminate per-spike full-memory accesses.
